name: Shebaniah
overview: Shebaniah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted in Scripture for his role as a trumpeter. His service as a trumpeter highlights a specific function within the Levitical duties, contributing to the worship and ceremonial life of Israel. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shebaniah appears as a proper name in Scripture without a provided meaning or divine origin. It is simply identified as the name of this Levitical trumpeter in 1 Chronicles 15:24.
familyAndRelationships: Shebaniah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe set apart for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are recorded in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Shebaniah's significance lies in his role as a trumpeter among the Levites, which was essential for the musical and liturgical functions during worship. His mention underscores the organized and divinely appointed structure of temple service in Israel. While brief, his inclusion in the biblical record affirms the importance of every role in the worship of the Lord.
